item.title: By: Carl Abbott
item.dc:creator: Carl Abbott
item.description:
I just noticed your reply Matthew. To answer your question, I would think it probably not particularly provable scientifically speaking. Science demands evidence, and for some aspect of reality, evidence will always be lacking. Yet, science has not found a way yet to acknowledge this. It helps to remember we are in the very early stages of the scientific era.
To be sure, considerable evidence is mounting up that confirms various aspects of this, but no overarching provable theory. And I doubt there ever will be.
Still, to me it is obvious, and I imagine it will be for anyone who can let go of the 'glory of humanity', so to speak. Thus, I guess in the future (10,000 CE?) the overall evidence will be insurmountable, and humanity will gradually accept the obvious. Until then the squabble will continue.

item.title: By: Matthew Costanzo
item.dc:creator: Matthew Costanzo
item.description: Hi. I agree with this article entirely. However, I'm a psychology graduate student and want to defend this position that the agricultural revolution led to the illusion of self and that this was the beginning of the dominoes that have fallen since. You don't have any citations for your assertions except the Tao and Hinduism. Would you by chance have come across any science that supports this position?
